title: Peanut Butter Overnight Oats
subtitle: Oats soaked overnight with peanut butter and banana
excerpt: Rolled oats left to soak overnight absorb the milk and yoghurt into something thick and creamy by morning. Peanut butter and banana make it filling enough to carry you to lunch. Mix it the night before and breakfast is already done.
sourceNotes: A modern no-cook breakfast method developed from the Bircher muesli tradition of soaking oats in liquid overnight. Peanut butter overnight oats became widely popular in the 2010s as a meal-prep staple.

recipe.batchNotes: Prepare up to 4 portions in individual jars. Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days without the banana topping.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Made the night before by design. Do not add banana until the morning.

content.text: Overnight oats are exactly what they sound like: rolled oats left in liquid from the evening so they soften gradually through the night, ready to eat cold the next morning. Adding {{peanut-butter}} peanut butter turns them into something properly sustaining, the fat and protein keep you full far longer than plain oats would. The only thing to get right is the ratio: too little milk and the oats stiffen up; too much and you end up with soup. 200 ml to 100 g of {{rolled-oats}} oats is the reliable starting point.

Put the {{rolled-oats}} rolled oats into a medium bowl or a jar with a lid. Pour in the {{whole-milk}} milk and spoon in the {{greek-yoghurt}} Greek yoghurt. Add the {{peanut-butter}} peanut butter and, if you want a touch of sweetness, the {{honey}} honey. Stir everything together until the peanut butter is fully incorporated, it can sit in streaks if you're not thorough, which means some spoonfuls are plain and some are very peanuty. A good stir now saves disappointment in the morning.

Cover the bowl or seal the jar and put it in the fridge. Eight hours is the sweet spot, long enough for the oats to fully absorb the liquid and soften through, short enough that they don't turn mushy. Overnight while you sleep is perfect.

In the morning, stir once more. The oats will have absorbed most of the liquid and thickened considerably. If they seem very stiff, loosen with a splash of milk. Slice the {{banana}} banana and lay it over the top. Serve straight from the fridge.
A handful of blueberries alongside the banana adds a sharp contrast to the richness.
Swap the honey for a teaspoon of maple syrup if you prefer a less floral sweetness.
A pinch of sea salt flakes over the top before eating sharpens the peanut flavour considerably.
Use almond butter or cashew butter in place of peanut butter for a milder, nuttier flavour.
Make 4 portions on Sunday and breakfast is sorted for most of the working week. Keep the banana separate until serving.
Too thick: add a splash more milk in the morning and stir well.
Too watery: use less milk next time, or add an extra tablespoon of yoghurt. Different brands of yoghurt vary in thickness.
Peanut butter not mixing in: warm it for 10 seconds in the microwave first to loosen it, then stir again.
